title: Beam crash leaves run marked 'running' forever; exception swallowed to stdout
description:
Run 90336412 (gen-11) stopped at 02:34:46 with status still 'running' and ended_at NULL.

CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (an earlier version of this issue blamed a Chez GC handshake; that was wrong — it profiled an unrelated process, /tmp/prog.clj, a core.async test spinning at 100%. Verified since: jolt honours deref timeouts on both futures and promises).

What actually happened: beam/run! threw. Evidence:
- harness (jolt serve, pid 62370) is IDLE — 10:37 CPU over 3h, no outbound sockets, no engine subprocesses
- ZERO swipl processes, though every live branch holds a prolog session -> run!'s finally ran and disposed them
- neither finish-run! call site (beam.clj:521 completed, :538 failed) was reached, since status is still 'running'

The swallow is api/control.clj start-run!:

  (catch Throwable e
    (log/error "run failed:" (ex-message e))
    {:status :error :error (ex-message e)})

It logs to the process's stdout (a tty) and returns a value nobody reads — the future's value is never dereferenced. The run row is never updated, (swap! active dissoc run-id) is skipped so abort! still thinks it is live, and nothing is journaled. The only record of the actual exception is a line in the user's terminal scrollback.

So a crash is indistinguishable from a healthy long-running round: same status, same absence of events. That is the real defect — not the underlying throw, which is still unidentified.
acceptance_criteria: A non-yielding branch turn forfeits within the deadline and the beam continues.
close_reason: Fixed in e0d30c3: run-rounds journals run-error and marks the row failed before rethrowing; start-run! drops the dead handle; runs/stalled? plus last_progress_at exposed on the run endpoint. Verified against the dead gen-11 run, which now reports stalled=true instead of claiming to be running.

title: Judge confirms SMT claims whose encoding doesn't match the claim text
description:
Gen-11 shipped three confirmed artifacts (P500 a#308, P600 a#313, P1000 a#311) asserting 'no subcollection satisfies the mod-3 layered necessary condition'. All three encode the WRONG condition: a modulus m divisible by 3 lands entirely inside one class mod 3, so its relative density in that class is 3/m, but all three encodings give it L/m (same coefficient as a coprime modulus) against a threshold of L. That understates 3-divisible contributions 3x, making the system strictly harder to satisfy, so unsat proves something weaker than the claim.

Verified with Z3 on a regenerated pool (identical moduli/lcm to the artifacts): as-encoded is unsat for N=300,315,500,600,1000; corrected (3L/m) is unsat for 300,315 and SAT for 500,600,1000. So the claims are false, not merely unsupported.

B1.3 diagnosed this itself and honourably abandoned rather than ship. The gate did not.

Root cause: nothing checks that the submitted encoding faithfully represents the claim text. The judge reads claim + verdict; the linter checks syntax. A mis-scaled coefficient is invisible to both.
acceptance_criteria: An encoding-faithfulness check exists that would reject these three artifacts; the three gen-11 artifacts are marked refuted/retracted in the journal.
notes:
Detection fixed in e0d30c3: verify_smt now sends every would-be confirmation to a judge that reads claim and encoding together and fails closed; refuted/ambiguous artifacts skip the call. Tests cover reject, accept, unparseable-fails-closed, and not-called-when-unconfirmed.

REMAINING: retracting the four bad gen-11 artifacts (a#308 P500, a#311 P1000, a#313 P600, a#316 pairwise-disjoint) from claim_status='confirmed'. A direct DB write was blocked by the permission classifier and needs the user's approval. Until then any run seeded from gen-11 via seed_run would import the false claims as established, since seed-from-run! selects on claim_status='confirmed'. gen-12 was therefore started with NO seed and hand-verified facts in the problem statement instead. a#315 (mod-5 layered on the 13-modulus exact-support set) was re-verified exhaustively and is SOUND; a#314 ('1 + 1 = 2') is true but trivial.

title: A shipped branch is never closed in the run record
description:
tools/done sets :status :done and :final-answer. Both DB-close paths in beam/run-loop miss that combination: the post-cull loop writes only branches with (not (:final-answer b)), and the run-end done-branch loop writes only (state/active? b) ones. So a branch that ships keeps status='active' in the branches table forever and never emits a branch-closed event.

Seen in gen-10 (05ecb88a): the run completed with all nine surviving branches shipped, and all nine still read 'active'. The GUI folds status from branch-closed events, so a finished run renders nine live branches, and the working indicator keys on :active too. Their engines are also held to run end instead of being disposed when the branch stops working.
close_reason: Closed

title: Erdos-Selfridge odd covering campaign: run generations 6-9
description:
STANDING INSTRUCTION (user, 2026-08-07): keep running seeded generations of the odd-covering campaign for at least 3-4 more rounds after gen-5, unless the $2000 problem is solved first.

Each round: wait for the current run to finish, verify its numbers by hand, update docs/odd-covering.md (frontier table + proofs), then launch the next generation with seed_run pointing at the run just finished, an ambition floor naming already-settled sets as unshippable, and targets chosen in Pareto-minimal order (maximize density slack, minimize lcm, minimize modulus count).

Run ids so far: c45ac428 (gen1), b84d2263 (gen2), 61de2075 (gen3), c5dcc35f (gen4), 7f4af6b7 (gen5, in flight).

STOP EARLY if: an actual odd distinct covering system is found and verified (then the work is verification and write-up, not another generation), or a generation returns nothing new AND leaves no usable direction - report that rather than burning another run.

The structural thread worth pushing: the entangled uncovered fraction is decaying slowly (17/45=0.378, 80/225=0.356, 47/135=0.348, 221/675=0.327). Does it decay to zero or hit a positive floor? A family-wide engine-confirmed lower bound would rule out odd coverings for infinitely many modulus sets at once - the strongest result this campaign could produce.
notes: gen8 74abc803 aborted at turn 184 (22 confirmed, journaled and seeded forward) to deploy the evolutionary loop. gen9 94452de2 is the first run with it: branch-out gate (reproduction on confirmation), crossover-block (children open holding every other lineage's confirmed results), stop-on-first-done? off (a ship no longer ends the run). Started at beam width 2 so growth has to be earned.
close_reason: gens 6-9 complete. gen9 produced the campaign's strongest result: a {3,5,7}-supported density-feasible set proved non-covering by a Lean-checked partition argument on a search space of 1.7e9 assignments. Evolutionary loop shipped and validated live (forked: 2).

title: Exhaustion progress report (never ship nothing)
description: UCLA Track B: when nothing ships, emit an honest structured progress report instead of a failure string - never ship nothing, never ship a lie. Extends the planned residual-objectives item: on beam exhaustion assemble per-branch undischarged thesis sub-claims, best confirmed artifacts with provenance, top shared-failure-log entries, and gate history summary, explicitly labeled not-a-solution. Do-not-claim-more-than-proved is mechanical for us: only engine-confirmed artifacts appear as established.
acceptance_criteria: Exhausted runs return structured report in message content + harness field: confirmed artifacts w/ provenance, undischarged sub-claims, relevant failures, labeled as progress report. No unconfirmed claim rendered as established (test). Bare beam-exhausted string gone.
close_reason: report assembly + rendering + API wiring + honesty tests; 100 tests green

title: Wind-down arbiter rung at late turn budget
description: UCLA reserves a deadline tail exclusively for assembly and shipping. Our 85% turn-budget notice informs but does not steer. Add an arbiter rung: at the late notice, the steer becomes assemble-and-ship-what-you-have (today only a human intervention example). Declares a prediction like other gates (branch calls audit or review within N turns) settled from the journal; sits below human directives and done-block in priority; one-shot re-fire guard.
acceptance_criteria: New gate in gates.edn with kind + doc. Arbiter rung with priority slot, prediction, re-fire guard. Prompt file for the steer. Test: scripted branch nearing cap receives exactly one wind-down steer, prediction settles; probe stays silent on a branch that ships early.
close_reason: wind-down gate, prompt, predictions, tests; 99 tests green

title: Audit restatement and is-relaxation axis
description: Audit must restate, self-contained, what the answer actually establishes (no anaphora), plus an is-relaxation flag comparing that against the pinned thesis - a failed attempt at the full claim is NOT a relaxation. Unlike UCLA we never re-pin the claim to the restatement (their ratchet let proofs pass against shrunken claims); drift is recorded against the original thesis. Claim-evidence gate extended: an artifact confirming only a weakened claim cannot substantiate the full answer, generalizing the existential bucket.
acceptance_criteria: Audit output schema carries restatement + is-relaxation. Anti-conflation rule in prompt. Thesis stays pinned; drift journaled. Claim-evidence gate refuses relaxation-only coverage; scripted transcript proves it. Existential-bucket tests still pass.
close_reason: ESTABLISHED/RELAXATION parsing, thesis-drift journal, done-gate relaxation refusal; 98 tests green

title: Named exemption lists in audit/review prompts
description: UCLA strictness was usable only because routine facts are exempted by name with DO-NOT-FLAG lists; without them the referee drowns everything in nitpicks and burns the done-block budget on non-gaps. Add named exemption lists to our audit/review prompt files (routine algebraic steps, standard library lemmas already engine-confirmed, phrasing/exposition items). Measure by max-done-blocks firings before/after on the probe set; the false-positive probe must still refuse.
acceptance_criteria: Exemption lists in prompt files as data-like sections. Probe set unchanged results for real gaps (false-positive probe still refuses; claim-evidence transcript still blocks). Bench note comparing done-block firings.
close_reason: exemption list wired to both judges + digest; 93 tests green

title: Judge-not-vote contract for verdict aggregation
description: Encode the UCLA consensus judge principle as a mechanical contract wherever more than one verdict about the same claim exists: LLM verdicts are evidence, never votes - no code path may majority-count them. Counting is legitimate only for independent engine confirmations (Prolog/Z3/Lean agreeing), which compose empirically. If multiple review/audit verdicts are ever aggregated, aggregation goes through a single judge that must record per-disagreement reasoning in the journal. Ship the contract and tests now so any future multi-model review lands inside it.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict-aggregation namespace with the contract in its docstring. Tests: aggregating N LLM verdicts by count throws or is unrepresentable; engine-confirmation counting allowed; judge path records reasoning per disagreement. Gate table untouched.
close_reason: consensus namespace + judge prompt + 7 contract tests; 89 tests green

title: Patch-existence severity criterion in audit/review
description: UCLA scorer_v4 core idea: a gap is BLOCKING only if the verifier cannot supply the concrete fix; if it can, the fix text must be included and the gap is minor - severity becomes operationally checkable and the refusal doubles as repair input. Apply to audit/review prompts: verdicts carry a gap list where each minor gap must embed its patch; done-refusal messages carry the patches so a refused turn is spent on repair, not re-diagnosis. Composes with max-done-blocks (each refusal costs a turn).
acceptance_criteria: Audit/review prompts restructured with MAJOR-iff-no-concrete-fix rule and mandatory patch text on minor gaps. verdict.clj parses gap+patch structure. done-refusal steer includes patches verbatim. Tests with corpus phrasings; probe transcript where a patchable gap does not block done but an unpatchable one does.
close_reason: MINOR/FIX parsing, fold-to-blocking rule, third disagreement direction, PATCHES in refusals; 91 tests green

title: Harden constrained-verdict contract in verdict.clj
description: Adopt the UCLA scorer_v4 findings as contract tests on the existing constrained-verdict layer. They independently abandoned a 1-10 score for a 3-class enum with fail-closed parsing, converging on our design; their additions we lack: (a) an anti-contradiction instruction in the audit/review prompts (a verdict of pass alongside a listed blocking gap is self-contradictory - pick the worse verdict), (b) a disagreement signal computed from the response text when the verdict line conflicts with the gap list, journaled like the auto-repaired signal rather than silently reconciled, with the verdict winning. Keep :unparseable failing closed.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt files updated with the anti-contradiction clause. New journal signal verdict-gap-disagreement computed from text, not parse path. Tests: verdict wins over gap list with signal recorded; unparseable still blocks done; existing verdict corpus passes unchanged.
close_reason: GAP lines, anti-contradiction clause, disagreement signal journaled; 82 tests green

title: Retry a __no_call__ turn with a doubled budget
description:
A branch that spends its whole output budget reasoning and never emits a tool call is a process failure, not evidence - the same thing vf-mti fixed for the judge, on the branch loop instead. Currently the turn is scored a failure, the harness appends 'Think less and call a tool', and the branch loses the turn.

Seen on gen-11 (90336412) turn 1: all three branches produced 48-51k characters, hit the 16384 cap, and called nothing. It self-corrects once conversation history exists (turn 3 was down to 4.7k), so the cost is a first-turn tax that scales with how dense the seeded brief is - and the brief gets denser every generation.

Fix: on __no_call__, retry once inside the same turn with a doubled max-tokens, journalled like judge-retry. Reuse the arithmetic-heavy sizing from tools/judge-max-tokens so a brief full of exact rationals opens high instead of paying for the doomed call first.

title: Start a new run from the GUI
description: The GUI can attach to a run, inspect branches and intervene, but there is no way to START one - a fresh run still needs a curl POST. Add a problem-statement input plus the run knobs (max turns, beam width, model, seed run) and POST /v1/runs from the GUI, then attach the poller to the new run id.
close_reason: Closed

title: Size the judge's token budget to the claim, not retry into it
description:
Measured on gen-10 (05ecb88a): audit/review are the beam's critical path. In rounds of width>=7 they were the straggler 24 of 28 times while taking ~24% of turns; verify_lean gated a round once in 47 turns and verify_smt never. 39 of the run's 46 judge-retries land after turn 40, when claims became exact-rational assertions over 20-26 moduli. The judge burns its output budget re-checking the arithmetic, hits the cap with no verdict, and is retried at doubled max-tokens - so an arithmetic-heavy audit costs 2-3 calls.

Fix: estimate the needed budget up front (claim length, count of rational literals / large denominators) and open the audit at the higher cap when it looks arithmetic-heavy, keeping retry as the fallback rather than the norm. Should cut the tail that sets round wall-clock while the other branches sit at the advance-all barrier.
close_reason: Closed

title: Critic scoring, Pareto retention, dynamic fork invitations
description: Replace the scalar-only cull with critic-scored Pareto retention and grow the beam on evidence. An LLM critic scores active branches on progress/momentum/distinctness/viability every critic-every turns (fail-closed parser, journaled). The scalar cull rule becomes the trigger; a triggered branch is culled only if dominated by a sibling, scored a dead end, or unscored - otherwise spared on a clock (cull-hard-multiple). The scheduler invites the strongest branch above the fork floor to branch_theses when the beam has room, so runs can start narrow and widen where verified progress is happening.
close_reason: landed with tests; 129 tests green

title: seed_run: import a prior run's confirmed artifacts into a new run's shared log
description: Cross-run campaigns currently pass findings by pasting them into the problem statement. Add seed_run to POST /v1/runs: copies the source run's engine-confirmed artifacts (claim + code) into the new run's shared_artifacts log with branch id prefixed seed:, so FTS context blocks serve them to branches. Seeding forces share-artifacts on for the run. Done gate still requires in-run re-verification, so inherited claims cannot ship on faith.

title: Resume with extended budget reopens exhausted branches
description: A run that exhausts max_turns is terminal today: resume keeps the ORIGINAL budget by design (anti-regrant after crash) and exhausted branches are inactive, so resume has nothing to advance. Add an explicit max_turns override to resume: raises the run row's budget, reopens branches closed as exhausted (culled/abandoned closed for cause stay closed), journals the extension. A human explicitly granting turns is not the crash-regrant hole.
close_reason: Closed

title: done requires retyping the audited answer verbatim; branches die reformatting it
description: Two consecutive live runs (magic-square 6a776cf5, Erdos-Straus f6377680) produced fully engine-confirmed results, got an audit PASS with an explicit approved answer, then died: the model calls done with the same content reformatted, the verbatim rule refuses, and the turn cap lands before a re-audit. The branch already stores the approved text (:last-audit). Proposal: done with the answer argument omitted ships exactly the last passing audit's approved answer; an explicitly supplied answer keeps the verbatim rule. Removes the transcription step without reopening the drift hole.
close_reason: done with no answer ships the last passing audit's approved text; explicit answers keep the verbatim rule

title: Judge hits token cap, audits come back unparseable
description: In the magic-square-of-squares live run (2026-08-06, run 6a776cf5), three audit calls at T25/T28/T29 returned 'unparseable - judge produced only reasoning and no answer, which usually means it hit the token cap while thinking'. Each cost a turn; the branch had an audit-approved answer at T30 but no turn left to call done, so the run exhausted one turn short of shipping. Consider a higher max-tokens for judge calls, a non-reasoning judge model, or retrying an unparseable verdict without charging the branch a turn.
close_reason: judge retries unparseable verdicts in-call with sharper instruction and doubled tokens; transport failures still fail closed

title: Journal-replay resume with persisted run anchor
description: UCLA crash recovery is event-sourced replay plus persisted run-start timestamp so restart does not re-grant budget. Our journal is already the event source written as-it-happens; resume is a replay fn reconstructing branch state (message history, gate counters, artifacts, turn counts) from SQLite. Persist run start + budget anchors in runs table; a resumed run continues within original budgets. Interventions pending at crash survive.
acceptance_criteria: Resume fn rebuilds branch state from journal; scripted run killed mid-flight resumes and completes within original turn budget (test). run-start anchor persisted, budget not re-granted. Pending interventions replayed. Aborted runs stay aborted.
close_reason: resume ns + run-rounds split + endpoint + tests; 112 tests green

title: Mechanical multi-candidate selection
description: UCLA needed an LLM selector ranking rigor/consistency/reliability with prefer-the-stronger-claim tiebreak because their candidates were prose. Ours are engine-audited, so selection is deterministic, no model in the path: slow-tier-confirmed beats fast-only, non-relaxation beats relaxation, higher claim-evidence coverage wins, earliest done-eligible breaks ties. Applies when several branches reach done-eligible states; ranking is journal-auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Pure ranking fn over branch results with documented key order; used when >1 done-eligible branch. Journal records ranking inputs+outcome. Property tests: slow>fast, full>relaxation, coverage ordering, deterministic tiebreak.
close_reason: rank-finished + select-done-branch + journal + tests; 110 tests green

title: Cross-branch dedup of slow verifications
description: UCLA claim-locking: atomic check-and-claim so two workers never verify the same statement concurrently; lock released on drafting failure, held on verdict failure. Ours: run-scoped registry keyed on normalized claim for SLOW-tier verifications only (fast checks stay duplicated - cheap and keeps independence). Second branch reaching the same claim waits or receives existing confirmed artifact with provenance rather than respending provider tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Registry with atomic claim semantics + release rules per UCLA (held while verdict pending, released on process failure). Applies to slow tier only. Test: two scripted branches verify same claim, one slow call, both credit artifact; journal records dedup hit.
close_reason: claim registry + review/verify_template wiring + journal + tests; 104 tests green

title: Shared confirmed-artifact log across branches

Add a run-scoped confirmed-artifact log, FTS5-ranked like the failure log, entries carrying branch + engine + claim. Safer than UCLA (engine-confirmed, not self-reported) but changes beam semantics - diversity may drop as branches converge on shared lemmas. Bears directly on the open beam-width question; sweep-widths is the instrument. Ship behind a flag, evaluate, keep only if width earns it.
acceptance_criteria: artifact log table + FTS5, write on confirmation, ranked retrieval into branch context behind config flag. Provenance survives round-trip. Journal shows cross-branch artifact hit in a beam test. sweep-widths runs flag on/off; results noted in bench.
